key_concept: In glycolysis, one molecule of glucose (6C) is split into two molecules of pyruvic acid (3C), so the pyruvate count is twice the glucose count.
steps: Glycolysis (EMP pathway) occurs in the cytoplasm and converts glucose into pyruvic acid.
Overall stoichiometry: $C_6H_{12}O_6 \rightarrow 2\,CH_3COCOOH$, i.e. 1 glucose (6C) gives 2 pyruvic acid (3C each).
Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate splits into two triose phosphates. Each triose phosphate is converted to one pyruvate.
For 206 glucose molecules: $206 \times 2 = 412$ molecules of pyruvic acid.
why_not_others: Option (1) 206 assumes 1 pyruvate per glucose, ignoring the 6C → 2 × 3C split. Option (3) 103 wrongly halves the number. Option (2) 309 has no stoichiometric basis.
common_trap: Students forget that each glucose yields two pyruvates, or they confuse this count with the net 2 ATP or 2 NADH produced per glucose.
time_saving_tip: Remember the rule 1 glucose = 2 pyruvate and simply double the given number.
